done_when: When a cold read or review loop stops, forge read, forge close, forge land and forge next print a ready-to-ask question that names the item in plain words and what it delivers, lists each open blocking note or finding as one plain sentence saying what goes wrong for whom, and says what accept, narrow and split would each concretely do for this item, and the guide tells the coordinator to ask exactly that

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `forge spec save` accepts story branches (`src/forge/records.py:364-375`), but this new `forge next` scan runs only for fix and forge worktrees. A spec stopped while being planned on a story branch has no question in `forge next`, so the owner cannot retrieve the question that `forge read` printed.
findings.title: Not done: stopped specs on story branches disappear from forge next

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The first-sentence cut discards the useful text after a short lead-in. For example, the existing spec at `docs/specs/agent-merge.md:22` starts its Behaviour with `**The owner's setting.**`; its question says only “The owner's setting” for what it delivers. A review body in the required form `Raise: Not done. <impact>` becomes only “not done” after this function strips `Raise:`. Both leave out context the owner needs to choose.
findings.title: Not done: stopped questions can omit the delivery or who is affected

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The shared question tells the owner that Narrow drops cases from the item's “Done when.” Specs instead have Behaviour and Acceptance criteria (`src/forge/records.py:86`). When a spec read stops, this is not a concrete description of what narrowing that spec would do.
findings.title: Not done: the narrow choice names a section specs do not have

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The named proofs do not cover these Done-when details. The close test supplies a body that already starts with an impact sentence, so it passes while a required-form `Raise: Not done. <impact>` body loses that impact. The read test uses a spec with a full-sentence Behaviour and creates specs only in fix worktrees; its `forge next` assertion never exercises a spec stopped on a supported story branch. It also asserts the invalid “Done when” wording for specs. The listed tests can pass with the question defects above.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

why: When a cold read or review loop stops, the owner is asked to accept, narrow or split with no context; with many items in parallel they can't tell what the item is or what was flagged
